diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy failures. The gate failed because of two distinct encoding-mismatch patterns plus a reasoning ambiguity. Check C1 (priority_order) failed in rollouts 0, 1, and 2 because the model placed FL-2 second and GEN-5 third (ordering by start time: FL-2 at 1200 vs GEN-5 at 1300) even though PF2 explicitly states GEN-5 must be the 'second board item'; only rollout 3 produced the expected [V-21, GEN-5, FL-2]. Check C5 (power-continuity check commitment) failed in rollouts 0, 1, and 3 because the model encoded the power-continuity check as commitment type 'pre_service_check' or embedded it inside a 'board_update' commitment rather than using the type 'power_continuity_check' that the check expects; only rollout 2 matched. Check C4 (dispatch hold commitment) failed in rollout 3 because that rollout folded the dispatch hold into a single 'board_update' commitment instead of emitting a separate 'dispatch_hold' commitment as rollouts 0, 1, and 2 did. No rollout auto-failed on the turn cap; all settled in 4 turns.

fix_instructions: The dominant failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH, driven by checks C4 and C5 expecting specific commitment type strings that the model does not consistently produce. (1) For C5: broaden the check to accept any commitment whose detail text mentions 'power-continuity' (or 'power continuity') regardless of the commitment type field, so that 'pre_service_check' and 'board_update' commitments containing that language also pass. Alternatively, add to the shared_context or settlement schema an explicit enumeration of required commitment types (e.g., 'dispatch_hold', 'power_continuity_check') so the model knows the exact type strings to emit. (2) For C4: similarly broaden the check to accept any commitment whose detail text mentions 'dispatch hold' rather than requiring a separate commitment with type 'dispatch_hold', or include the required commitment-type enumeration in the settlement instructions. (3) For C1: the model in 3 of 4 rollouts ordered items by start time rather than by the positional constraint in PF2 ('second board item'). Either tighten the reveal text for PF2 to explicitly state 'GEN-5 is position 2 in priority_order; FL-2 moves to position 3' so the model cannot interpret 'second board item' as chronological, or loosen C1 to accept [V-21, FL-2, GEN-5] when the time windows are individually correct and non-conflicting, since the model's time-based ordering is a reasonable operational interpretation.
